full_judgment: 7. Mr. A.S.M. Khalequzzaman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in considering that the plaintiffs are the executants of the kabala in question and therefore very much party to the document and without a prayer for cancellation of the deed on payment of ad valorem court fees the suit for simple declaration is not maintainable and hence the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the High Court Division and the Courts below concurrently committed an error in holding that the suit as filed on 04.01.1998 for declaration regarding the kabala No.4995 dated 23.11.1988 executed by the plaintiffs is not barred by the limitation and the simple suit for declaration without canceling the deed on payment of ad valorem court fees is not maintainable at all and hence the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He submitted that the suit property is the homestead of the petitioner and the respondents in their respective shares pursuant to the kabala in question and the same is the only property of the petitioner and source of income for maintenance of the petitioner's family. The opposite party by taking a false plea has been trying to make the petitioner destitute. The trial Court utterly failed to appreciate the cunning device of the opposite party and has come to a wrong finding stating the kabala in question as jimma deed and as such the judgment and decree suffers from illegality and hence liable to be set aside.
